result.note: Tests the venue of the August 2026 Saudi–Turkey–Pakistan collective defence pact and its key terms and background.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a trilateral collective defence agreement. In which city was it signed?
questions.explain: The agreement was signed in Mecca on Friday 7 August 2026. New Delhi said it is following the agreement closely, having earlier warned that Saudi-Pakistani defence cooperation could affect Indian security.
questions.source: Signed in Mecca on Friday, the agreement says an armed attack on one will be treated as an attack on all three.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the defence agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan in August 2026:
items: It provides that an armed attack on any one of the three will be treated as an attack on all three.
The precise military obligations of each signatory have been made public.
It builds on a bilateral defence pact that Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed in September 2025.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the story says the precise military obligations remain undisclosed. Turkey's entry adds NATO's second-largest military and a defence industry already supplying Saudi drones.
questions.source: The precise military obligations remain undisclosed.
